flags.title: Formal DIAGNOSES section is blank
flags.action: Populate the DIAGNOSES/Assessment section with a formal diagnosis list; do not leave it blank with diagnoses embedded only in the treatment plan narrative.
flags.body: The DIAGNOSES header is present but contains no entries — the note goes directly from 'DIAGNOSES:' to 'TREATMENT PLAN:'. All diagnostic information is embedded in the treatment plan paragraph, which is non-standard and creates audit exposure. Per ICD-10-CM Sec IV.A, the first-listed diagnosis must be identifiable from the medical record; having diagnoses only in prose within a plan section complicates coding attestation and payer review. For workers' compensation claims specifically, a blank Assessment is a documentation deficiency that can delay or deny claim processing.
flags.guideline_reference: ICD-10-CM Sec IV.A; Ortho pack §15 (Assessment checklist); AHIMA/ACDIS 2026 §1

flags.action: Add Y99.0 (civilian work status) to the code table immediately; obtain and document mechanism, workplace location, and activity details to complete the W/X, Y92, and Y93 external-cause code set.
flags.body: This is a provider-confirmed workers' compensation injury (D/I: 11/13/2025; Dr. Sabbag explicitly documents work-relatedness and files for retroactive WC authorization). ICD-10-CM Sec I.C.20 and Ortho pack §9 require four external-cause elements for work injuries: mechanism (W00–X58), place of occurrence (Y92.x), activity (Y93.x), and work/employment status (Y99.0). None of the four appear in the code table. Y99.0 can be added immediately from existing documentation. The mechanism, place, and activity codes require additional note documentation (see flag-005).

flags.title: ROM not in degrees; JAMAR deferred — OT defense incomplete
flags.action: Document left wrist ROM in degrees for flexion, extension, radial deviation, and ulnar deviation; record JAMAR grip strength or document a clinical rationale for bilateral deferral.
flags.body: The note documents 'limited active range of motion of the left wrist in flexion, extension, and lateral deviation' and notes motion is decreased from preinjury baseline, but provides no degree measurements. Ortho pack §11 requires ROM in specific degrees, not qualitative descriptors, when the chief complaint is mobility or pain. The JAMAR dynamometer was also deferred for both hands without a stated reason. Quantified ROM and grip strength are essential to defend the occupational therapy authorization request (2x/week for 3 weeks) and to satisfy workers' compensation functional-impairment documentation standards; qualitative terms alone are insufficient for medical necessity defense.
flags.guideline_reference: Ortho pack §11 (functional impairment quantification); Ortho pack §10 (authorization defense documentation)
flags.reimbursement_impact: Quantified ROM deficits and grip strength strengthen the medical-necessity narrative for the OT authorization; unquantified deficits increase risk of therapy authorization denial.

flags.title: 99215 referenced; documented MDM supports 99214 at most
flags.action: Add documentation of a High-MDM driver (e.g., prescription drug management, independent imaging interpretation, or external physician discussion) to support 99215, or adjust the billed level to 99214.
flags.body: The note contains '[.KS15 — 99215 Level-of-Service billing paragraph]', indicating 99215 billing. Under AMA 2021 MDM rules, 99215 (established patient) requires ≥2 of 3 elements at High MDM. Scoring this encounter: (1) Problems = Moderate — one acute complicated post-surgical injury with WC authorization complications does not reach 'threat to life or bodily function'; (2) Data = Low — no documented independent interpretation of an outside test, no documented external physician consultation, minimal Category 1 items; (3) Risk = Moderate — the WC authorization dispute significantly limiting treatment initiation qualifies as social determinants of health restricting management (a 2021 Moderate-Risk driver). Two-of-3 at Moderate supports 99214. No element reaches High. Billing 99215 without High-MDM documentation creates recoupment exposure.
flags.guideline_reference: em_mdm_2021.md — AMA 2021 Office/Outpatient E/M MDM grid; CMS MLN E/M documentation guidance
flags.reimbursement_impact: Documented MDM (Moderate Problems + Low Data + Moderate Risk via SDOH) supports 99214, not 99215; billing 99215 creates audit and recoupment exposure for the underdocumented level differential.

flags.title: Work injury mechanism, location, and activity undocumented

flags.body: The note confirms work-relatedness of the 11/13/2025 left distal radius fracture but never states how the fracture occurred, where in the workplace it happened, or what the patient was doing at the time. Without this documentation, three of the four required WC external-cause code elements (mechanism W00–X58, place Y92.x, activity Y93.x) cannot be coded. Incomplete external-cause coding on a WC claim undermines the injury record and may trigger adjuster requests for clarification or claim reprocessing. Per ICD-10-CM Sec I.C.20, mechanism and work-relatedness must be provider-documented; patient report alone is insufficient.

flags.title: Fracture pattern unspecified — more specific sequela code possible
flags.action: Clarify the fracture pattern of the left distal radius fracture (Colles', Smith's, Barton's, or other) to enable a more specific sequela code in place of S52.502S.
flags.body: S52.502S (unspecified fracture of lower end of left radius, sequela) is valid as coded, but ICD-10-CM Sec I.B.2 requires coding to the highest specificity the documentation supports. ORIF is the standard treatment for displaced distal radius fractures; the fracture pattern (Colles', Smith's, Barton's, or other) determines the more specific code. The fracture pattern is likely documented in the original emergency or operative report from November 2025 but is not referenced in this note. Colles' fracture (dorsal displacement) is the most common distal radius fracture pattern requiring ORIF and would be coded S52.532S.
flags.guideline_reference: ICD-10-CM Sec I.B.2 (specificity mandate); Ortho pack §3 (fracture coding); Ortho pack §13
